definitions.explanation: A period of time granted before something must be done or before a decision takes effect. Often used in legal and official contexts for extensions, deferrals, or probation.

examples.english: There is no more time to spare.

examples.japanese: {支払|しはら}いの{猶予|ゆうよ}を{認|みと}めてもらった。
examples.english: I was granted a grace period for payment.

examples.japanese: {懲役|ちょうえき}3{年|ねん}、{執行|しっこう}{猶予|ゆうよ}5{年|ねん}の{判決|はんけつ}が{言|い}い{渡|わた}された。
examples.english: A sentence of three years imprisonment, suspended for five years, was handed down.

notes:
USAGE:
Functions as a noun and suru-verb. In legal contexts, {執行|しっこう}{猶予|ゆうよ} means a suspended sentence — the prison term is deferred on condition of good behavior. In everyday language, {猶予|ゆうよ}がない means there is no time to waste or no room for delay.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {執行|しっこう}{猶予|ゆうよ}: suspended sentence
- {猶予|ゆうよ}{期間|きかん}: grace period
- {猶予|ゆうよ}がない: no time to spare
- {猶予|ゆうよ}を{与|あた}える: to grant a reprieve
- {支払|しはら}いの{猶予|ゆうよ}: payment deferral
